newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Treasuries close thin session sharply higher.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Treasuries close thin session sharply higher.

text.p: U.S. Treasuries ended an abbreviated and quiet session sharply higher Friday, as the market picked up where it left off before Thanksgiving.
The 6-1/2 percent 30-year bond was at 101-27/32, up 30/32 from late Wednesday. Its yield fell to 6.36 percent from 6.43 percent -- its lowest level since closing at 6.34 percent March 4.
"You have got to be impressed with the market's performance," said a bond trader at a primary dealership. "The trend remains that we have better buyers."

Trading activity was said to be very thin, as most trading desks operated with skeleton staffs. A large number of traders took the day off in order to extend their Thanksgiving holiday through the weekend.
"You could throw a grenade in here and not hurt anyone," mused a trader at a primary dealership.
By midday, volume slowed to a trickle and traders at smaller firms said they saw no flows at all. Traders noted that large swings are common when liquidity is thin.
PSA The Bond Market Trade Association had recommended an early close at 1400 EST/1900 GMT.
The market was higher before the U.S. session began, as a spate of buying by Japanese accounts pushed Treasuries up as much as 3/8-point during Tokyo trading.
But some profit-taking early in the U.S. session brought Treasuries off their highs.
The market briefly moved back toward pre-Thanksgiving levels after shrugging off a 0.5 percent rise in personal spending and unchanged personal income in October.
Yet, a strengthening dollar, a German bund rally to record highs, traditional month-end buying and short-covering gave Treasuries a big bounce, traders said.
Nelson Thomson, head trader at Yamaichi International (America) Inc, noted that much of the market's success this session was due to "carryover" from European markets.
In particular, German DTB futures ended trade just shy of an all-time high, reached earlier in the day.

Treasuries also got a boost from the December bond contract breaking above Wednesday's high of 116-5/32. One trader said that many technicians had recommended selling above 116. Late Friday, it was at 116-8/32, suggesting very bullish sentiment, players said.

Meanwhile, a fall in the APICS manufacturing index to 46.8 percent in November from October's 49.1 percent added to the positive market tone. Some traders also cited a rise in the Lehman Brothers market index as helping to boost bonds.
The two-year note closed at 100-2/32, up 4/32. Its yield fell to 5.59 percent from 5.66 percent. The 10-year note rose 17/32 to 103-9/32, while its yield declined to 6.05 percent from 6.12 percent.
The market next eyes the National Association of Purchasing Management November survey, due Monday morning.
